Rashi on Pesachim 17a:10:1.hebrew: ויען חגי ויאמר וגו' - סיפיה דקרא: "וכן כל מעשה ידיהם, ואשר יקריבו שם טמא הוא":
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:10:1.english: And Haggai answered and said, etc. - The end of the verse [is]: “And so is all the work of their hands, and that which they offer there is impure.”

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:10:2.hebrew: בשלמא לרב - דאמר אישתבש כהני, היינו דקרי למעשה ידיהם טמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:10:2.english: Granted, according to Rav - Since he said [that] the priests erred, that is why [the verse] calls the work of their hands impure.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:11:1.hebrew: איתמוהי קא מתמה - מאחר שבקיאין הן בהלכות טומאה, וכי כל מעשה ידיהם טמא הוא?:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:11:1.english: He is expressing bewilderment - Since they are knowledgeable in the laws of impurity, is all the work of their hands impure?

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:11:2.english: And so - Does not imply a question.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:11:3.english: That they corrupted their deeds - [The prophet] was prophesying for a later time, that they would corrupt their deeds during the Second Temple with other sins.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:13:1.hebrew: וללוי - דתני מדבחיא, והכא כתיב יין ושמן דמטמאו — הא ניחא אי סבר ליה בהא מילתא כשמואל, ד"דכן" דיוסף בן יועזר — "דכן מלטמא אחרים" הן, אבל טומאת עצמן יש בהן; משכחת לה להאי דכתיב: "אם יגע טמא נפש בכל אלה", דקאמר "יטמא" — דנגעו כולהו בראשון, ולאו אסדרא קמא נקט, ולא אישתבש כהני. שבתחלה שאלם על הסדר, ואמרו לו על האחרון "לא יטמא", מפני שהיין לא יכול לטמאו לשמן, שאין משקין בי מדבחיא מטמאין שום דבר; ולבסוף שאלם אם יגע הטמא עצמו בכל אלה, כלומר: או בזה או בזה, ואמרו ליה "יטמא":
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:13:1.english: And according to Levi - For he teaches [that the testimony applies to liquids of the] altar, and here it is written "wine" and "oil," which became impure — this works out well if he holds in this matter in accordance with Shmuel, that the "pure" of Yosef ben Yo’ezer [means that] they are pure from transmitting impurity to others, but they themselves are susceptible to impurity; you can find [a scenario] for that which is written: "If one who is impure by a corpse touches any of these," where it says "it shall be impure" — that they all touched a [source of] first-[degree impurity], and [the prophet] was not following the first order, and the priests did not err. For initially, he asked them in sequence, and they said to him regarding the last [item], "It shall not be impure," because the wine could not transmit impurity to the oil, as liquids of the altar do not transmit impurity to anything; and ultimately he asked them if the impure [person] himself touches any of these — that is to say, either this [item] or that [item] — and they said to him, "It shall be impure."

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:14:1.hebrew: אלא אי סבר ליה כרב דאמר דכן ממש היכי משכחת לה - להאי ״יטמא״ דקרא? בשלמא לרב גופיה לא קשיא, דאיהו תני ״מטבחיא״; אלא ללוי קשיא:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:14:1.english: However, if he holds in accordance with Rav, who said [that they are] actually pure, under what circumstances can you find it - [Namely,] this [statement of] "it shall become impure" in the verse? Granted, for Rav himself it is not difficult, as he taught [the version]: "the slaughterhouse"; but for Levi it is difficult.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:15:1.hebrew: ולשמואל - דאמר: לא אישתבש, ופריש למילתיה משום דחמישי הוה השמן, דמה שנגע בכנפו כתיב. הא אי רביעי הוה האי שמן — הוה טמא, ואע"ג דמן היין קבלה; אלמא: משקין מטמאין אחרים:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:15:1.english: And according to Shmuel - Who said [that the priests] did not err, and explained his position [that their answer was correct] because the oil was [of the] fifth [degree of impurity], as it is written that [it was] that which touched with its corner [that touched the bread]. It follows that had this oil been [of the] fourth [degree], it would have been impure, even though it received [its impurity] from the wine; this proves that liquids transmit impurity to other [items].

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:15:2.hebrew: הא ניחא - אי תנא בעדותו של יוסף משקה מטבחיא, אבל משקה מדבחיא אפילו אחריני נמי מטמאו — היינו דפריש למילתיה לעיל, ואמר: האי דלא הוי שיבוש משום דחמישי הוה, והיין שהוא רביעי לא עביד ליה חמישי; הא אי הוה יין שלישי, הוה עביד ליה רביעי. אלא אי תנא מדבחיא, כלוי — מאי איריא דפריש לעיל משום דחמישי הוה? אפילו אי הוה יין שני, שלישי לשמן לא עביד:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:15:2.english: This works out well - If he taught in the testimony of Yose [ben Yo'ezer]: "The liquids of the slaughterhouse," but [held that] the liquids of the altar transmit impurity even to other [items] as well — that is why he explained his statement above and said: The reason that [their answer] was not an error was because [the oil] was fifth [degree], and the wine, which is fourth [degree], does not render it fifth [degree]; whereas if the wine had been third [degree], it would have rendered it fourth [degree]. However, if he taught "liquids of the altar," like Levi — why did he specifically explain above that it was because it was fifth [degree]? Even if the wine had been second [degree], it would not have rendered the oil third [degree]!

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:15:3.hebrew: משקי בי מדבחיא - כלומר, כל אלו של קודש נקראין על שם מזבח, כגון: דם לזריקה, ומים ויין לנסך, ושמן למנחות:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:15:3.english: Liquids of the altar - That is to say, all these [liquids] of sacred items are called by the name of the altar, such as blood for sprinkling, and water and wine for libation, and oil for meal offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:17:1.hebrew: שנטמאו בפנים - בעזרה. והוציאן לחוץ, ונפסלו ביוצא — שאין ראויין עוד למזבח:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:17:1.english: That became ritually impure inside - In the Courtyard. And [one] took them outside, and they were disqualified as [having been taken] outside [yotzei], as they are no longer fit for the altar.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:17:2.hebrew: טהורין - מלטמא אחרים, שהרי לא ירדה להן תורת טומאה מתחלה לטמא אחרים, והן עצמן ודאי טמאין כנבואת חגי:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:17:2.english: [They are] pure - From transmitting impurity to other [items], for the status of ritual impurity did not initially descend upon them to transmit impurity to other [items]; and they themselves are certainly impure, in accordance with the prophecy of Haggai.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:17:3.hebrew: אבל נטמאו בחוץ - קודם שיהא שם מדבחיא עליהן, והכניסן לפנים — טמאין, ואפילו לטמא אחרים; דטומאתן כבר ירדה בהן, ומי הפקיעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:17:3.english: However, [if] they became impure outside - Before the designation of altar [liquids] was upon them, and one brought them inside — [they are] impure, and even to defile other [items]; for their impurity had already descended upon them, and who revoked it?

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:18:1.hebrew: איני - ארישא פריך, דקתני: הוציאן לחוץ — טהורין, ולא אמרינן תחול טומאתן למפרע:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:18:1.english: Is that so? - [The Gemara] raises an objection against the first clause [of the baraita], which teaches: [If] one took them outside, they are pure, and we do not say that their impurity should take effect retroactively.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:18:2.english: Only in their place - Inside [the Temple].

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:18:3.hebrew: לא למעוטי נטמאו בחוץ והכניסן לפנים - כדמתרץ לישנא בסיפא דמילתא, דהכי משמע: אלא כשנטמאו במקומן. ומשום דלא סיימיה לפרושא דמילתא, פריך ליה: והא במקומן קאמר, דמשמע: כל זמן שהן במקומן טהורין, ותו לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:18:3.english: No, to exclude [liquids that] became impure outside and one brought them inside - As [the Gemara] resolves the phrasing at the conclusion of the matter, that this is what it means: [the Sages said they are pure] only when they became impure in their place. And because it had not [yet] finished explaining the matter, it challenges this: But didn't he say "in their place"?! which implies that as long as they are in their place they are pure, and no more.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:1:2.hebrew: אישתבש כהני - שטהרו רביעי בקודש. אלמא יין ושמן — דמשקי בית מטבחיא נינהו — ומיטמאו. ואי טומאת משקין דרבנן, הא אמרת דלא גזור עלייהו! ואי נמי בטומאות דרבנן קא בדיק להו חגי לכהני, וכבר נגזר טומאה על המשקין בימי חגי הנביא שהיה מאנשי כנסת הגדולה — קשיא לרב, דהא אמר: דכן ממש. וכ"ש אי בדאורייתא קא משתעי, קשיא לרב. והא ליכא למימר מדרבנן ודלא כיוסף בן יועזר, דאקרא לא פליג, דמשמע דאית עלייהו טומאה — אי דאורייתא אי דרבנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:1:2.english: The priests erred - In that they declared a fourth [degree of impurity] in consecrated [food] pure. Evidently, wine and oil — which are liquids of the slaughterhouse — become impure! And if the impurity of liquids is rabbinic, didn't you say that they did not decree [impurity] upon them? Or, even if Haggai was testing the priests regarding rabbinic impurities, and impurity had already been decreed upon liquids in the days of Haggai the prophet, who was of the Men of the Great Assembly — it is difficult for Rav, who said: '[They are] actually pure'! And all the more so if [Scripture] is speaking of [impurity] by Torah law, it is difficult for Rav. And one cannot say [that this defilement is only] rabbinic and does not accord with Yosef ben Yo'ezer, for [Yosef ben Yo'ezer] would not dispute Scripture, which indicates that they are subject to impurity, whether by Torah law or rabbinically.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:1:3.hebrew: מידי הוא טעמא אלא לרב - כלום אתה מקשה אלא לרב? רב, לא קשיא ליה האי: לעולם חגי בדרבנן בדיק להו, וכבר נגזרה גזירת הטומאה על המשקין. ולרב, אליבא דיוסף בן יועזר לא תיקשי, דרב משקי בי מטבחיא תני בעדותו של יוסף — משקה המטבחים, דם ומים; אבל משקה מדבחיא — היין והשמן, שהם משקה המזבח — גזרו רבנן טומאה עלייהו. והיינו דבסדר טומאות דהאי קרא איכא אוכל מטמא אוכל, ומשק' מטמא משקה, דמדרבנן טומאה עושה כיוצא בה:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:1:3.english: Is the reason anything other than according to Rav? - Are you raising an objection at all except according to Rav? For Rav, this is not difficult: actually, Haggai was examining them regarding rabbinic [law], and the decree of impurity upon liquids had already been enacted. And for Rav, according to [the testimony of] Yosef ben Yo’ezer, it is not difficult, for Rav teaches “liquids of the slaughterhouse” in the testimony of Yosef — [meaning] the liquids of the slaughterhouse, [namely] blood and water; but [as for] the liquids of the altar — the wine and the oil, which are the liquids of the altar — the Rabbis decreed impurity upon them. And that is why in the order of impurities of this verse, there is food rendering food impure and liquid rendering liquid impure, for by rabbinic law, impurity produces its like.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:6:1.hebrew: מי כתיב ונגע כנפו - אל הלחם, דמשמע שהשרץ נגע בלחם, דלחם הוי ראשון? מה שנגע בכנפו נגע ללחם, דה"ל לחם שני:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:6:1.english: Is it written: “And its corner touched” - “unto the bread,” which would imply that the creeping animal touched the bread, so that the bread is [a] first [degree of impurity]? [Rather,] that which touched its corner touched the bread, so that the bread is [a] second [degree of impurity].

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:7:1.hebrew: טמא נפש - קס"ד טמא מת, שהוא אב הטומאה כשרץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:7:1.english: One who is impure with [impurity imparted by] a corpse - It enters [the Gemara's] mind [that this means] one defiled by a corpse, who is a primary source of ritual impurity like a creeping animal.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:7:2.hebrew: בכל אלה - כסדר שפירשנו — טמא מת בלחם, ולחם בנזיד, וכו':
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:7:2.english: In all these - In the order that we explained: one impure from a corpse [touches] the bread, and the bread [touches] the stew, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:7:3.hebrew: מדהכא לא אישתבש - דאמרו ליה: רביעי טמא, כדכתיב: "ויאמרו יטמא" — הכא נמי לא אישתבש, ואיהו במה שנגע בכנפו אמר להו, דה"ל שמן חמישי, ומשום הכי אמרי ליה: טהור. אלא לרב, דאמר: גבי שרץ נמי רביעי בעא מינייהו — מאי שנא דאמרו ליה: טהור:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:7:3.english: From [the fact] that here they did not err - For they said to him [that a] fourth [degree of impurity] is impure, as it is written: “And they said: It shall be impure”; [there] too they did not err, as he, [referring to] that which touched the corner of his garment, spoke to them, which made the oil a fifth [degree], and because of this they said to him: “[It is] pure.” But according to Rav, who said that regarding the creeping animal he also asked them about a fourth [degree], what is different that they said to him: “[It is] pure”?

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:8:1.hebrew: בקיאין הן בטומאת מת - ויודעים שהשלישי עושה בה רביעי, ולא היו בקיאין בטומאת שרץ, וסבורין שאין שלישי עושה בה רביעי:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:8:1.english: They were experts in the impurity of a corpse - And [they] knew that a third [degree] produces a fourth [degree] in it; but they were not experts in the impurity of a creeping animal, and thought that a third [degree] does not produce a fourth [degree] in it.

Rashi on Pesachim 17a:9:1.hebrew: רבינא אמר - לא היו בקיאין ברביעי בקודש כלל, וגבי מת שלישי בקודש בעא מינייהו; דהאי טמא נפש דקרא לאו טמא מת, אלא מת ממש — כלומר, טומאת נפש. ומת — אבי אבות, ולחם — אב, ונזיד — ראשון, ויין — שני, ושמן — שלישי:
Rashi on Pesachim 17a:9:1.english: Ravina said - They were not knowledgeable regarding fourth-[degree impurity] in consecrated [items] at all, and regarding a corpse, he was asking them [about] third-[degree impurity] in consecrated [items]; for this "one defiled by a corpse" in the verse is not [someone] defiled by a corpse, but an actual corpse — that is to say, the impurity of a corpse. And a corpse [is] an ultimate primary source [of impurity], and bread [is] a primary source, and stew [has] first-degree [impurity], and wine [has] second-degree [impurity], and oil [has] third-degree [impurity].

Tosafot on Pesachim 17a:3:1.hebrew: רביעי בקודש בעא מינייהו - פ"ה דנגע בכנפו היינו שרץ אל הלחם, והלחם אל הנזיד, וכו'. וקשה לר"ת: דמאי שנא ד"ואל כל מאכל" יהיה פירוש "או אל כל מאכל" יותר מכולם? ועוד, למה דחק שמואל לתרץ במה שנגע בכנפו? לימא "אל כל מאכל" דוקא! ועוד, למה קורא הכתוב לשרץ כנף? ועוד, דמפרש רבינא התם: רביעי בקדש, הכא: שלישי — שהלחם נעשה אב הטומאה כשנוגע במת, והא קיימא לן בהמפלת (נדה כח:) דכל דבר שאין לו טהרה במקוה אינו נעשה אב הטומאה! מיהו יש לומר, ד"אין נעשה אב הטומאה" היינו דווקא לטמא אדם וכלים, אבל לאוכלין ומשקין נעשה אב הטומאה. ומפר"ת: דהשרץ נגע בכנף ונעשה ראשון, והכנף אל הלחם או אל הנזיד, וחד מהנך אל היין או אל השמן — הרי שלשה, "ואל כל מאכל" — הרי ארבעה; ונקט סדר כנף, מאכל, משקה, מאכל — דלא בעי למינקט שיעשה כיוצא בו. ולשמואל דייק מדכתיב בכנפו — הרי חמש. והשתא אתי שפיר לרבינא, דאמר: הכא שלישי — שהכנף הנוגע במת נעשה אב הטומאה, כדין כל הכלים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 17a:3:1.english: Fourth-[degree impurity] in consecrated items he raised as a dilemma before them - Rashi explained that "and it touched with his corner" means [that the] creeping animal [touched] the bread, and the bread [touched] the stew, etc. And Rabbeinu Tam finds it difficult: For what is different [about the phrase] "and to any food" that it should be interpreted as "or to any food" more than all the others? And furthermore, why did Shmuel exert himself to explain [that it touched] "with that which touched his corner"? Let him say that "and to any food" is [counted] specifically! And furthermore, why does Scripture call the creeping animal a "corner"? And furthermore, for Ravina explains: There, [the dilemma concerned] fourth-[degree impurity] in consecrated items; here, [it concerned] third-[degree impurity], as the bread becomes a primary source of ritual impurity [av hatumah] when touching [one contaminated by] a corpse. And yet we hold in [the chapter entitled] HaMappelet (Niddah 28b) that anything that cannot be purified in a ritual bath does not become a primary source of ritual impurity! However, one could say that "it does not become a primary source of ritual impurity" applies specifically to conferring impurity upon a person and vessels, but with respect to food and drink, it does become a primary source of ritual impurity. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that the creeping animal touched the corner [of the garment], and [the corner] became [an item with] first-degree [impurity]; and the corner [touched] the bread or the stew, and one of these [touched] the wine or the oil — behold, [that is] three; "and to any food" — behold, [that is] four. And [Scripture] formulated the sequence [as] corner, food, drink, food, because it did not want to cite [a case where an item] renders [another item] like itself. And according to Shmuel, he deduces from that which is written "with his corner" [that] behold, [there are] five. And now, [the matter] works out well according to Ravina, who said: Here [it is] third-[degree impurity], since the corner [of the garment] that touches a corpse becomes a primary source of ritual impurity, in accordance with the law of all vessels:
